claim_as_written: IP3R is the ER's ligand-gated Ca2+-release channel; PLC cleaves PIP2 to IP3, IP3 binds the N-terminal core, the channel opens and releases Ca2+ from the ER
note: Streb 1983 established IP3-evoked release from a non-mitochondrial store; Furuichi 1989 cloned the receptor; Ferris 1989 showed the purified receptor alone conducts Ca2+; Bosanac 2002 solved the N-terminal IP3-binding core with ligand bound, and Bosanac 2005 [R06] the suppressor domain that tunes its affinity.

claim_as_written: It is the origin of most agonist-evoked cytosolic Ca2+ signals in non-muscle cells - puffs, oscillations and waves
note: The elementary event (puff) and the oscillation/wave hierarchy are established (Yao 1995; Berridge 1993). "Most ... in non-muscle cells" is a review-level generalisation, not a measured fraction; it is not quantified anywhere and must not be quoted as a number.

claim_as_written: IP3R mediates ER-to-mitochondrion Ca2+ transfer at MAM contact sites, setting the threshold for apoptosis
note: Rizzuto 1998 showed close ER-mitochondria contacts determine mitochondrial Ca2+ responses; Csordas 2006 measured the linkage; Pinton 2008 reviews the apoptotic threshold; Bartok 2019 shows the three IP3R isoforms differ in this role - relevant to S17/S22.

claim_as_written: Gating is co-agonist: IP3 alone does not open the channel, and the Ca2+ dependence is biphasic (low activates, high inhibits)
note: Bezprozvanny 1991 is the bell-shaped Ca2+ response; Marchant 1997 showed sequential IP3-then-Ca2+ binding; Alzayady 2016 showed all four IP3-binding sites must be occupied to open the channel.

claim_as_written: ATP, PKA/PKC phosphorylation, Bcl-2-family proteins, IRBIT and ERp44 all modulate the receptor
note: One primary source per modulator: ATP (Bezprozvanny 1993), PKA phosphorylation (Supattapone 1988), Bcl-2 (Chen 2004), IRBIT (Ando 2003), ERp44 (Higo 2005). PKC was not separately verified and is dropped from the statement.

claim_as_written: The subunit assembles as a homotetramer (~1.2 MDa) with a large cytosolic mushroom cap over a small membrane domain
note: Maeda 1990 purified the tetrameric complex; Fan 2015 and Baker 2021 are the cryo-EM reconstructions showing the cytosolic cap over the small TM domain. The mass figure needs care: the background document says ~1.2 MDa, the primary structural paper [R22] says 1.3 MDa, and 4 x 2758 aa (Q14643) is ~1.25 MDa. All three are the same number rounded differently; quote 1.3 MDa with [R22] or the arithmetic with the accession, never ~1.2 MDa unattributed.

claim_as_written: The pore lies between TM5 and TM6 with a short selectivity filter; the C-terminal tail after TM6 runs back up into the cytosolic domain and couples ligand binding to the gate
note: Fan 2015/2018, Paknejad 2018 and Baker 2021 all resolve the TM5-TM6 pore, the selectivity filter and the C-terminal helix returning into the cytosolic domain as the allosteric coupling path.

claim_as_written: C-terminal variants can be dominant-negative in a tetramer
note: McEntagart 2016 demonstrated a dominant-negative effect for de novo ITPR1 channel-domain variants; Molitor 2024 demonstrated the same for ITPR3 p.Arg2524Cys. Both are C-terminal/pore-proximal.
Re-derived from Ensembl (release 15.12) in results/s0_baseline/gene_structure.tsv: all three cytogenetic bands confirmed exactly. No longer a literature claim.

claim_as_written: Tissue emphasis: ITPR1 cerebellar Purkinje cells and broad; ITPR2 broad, secretory epithelia, glia; ITPR3 epithelial/secretory, pancreas, liver
note: Supported qualitatively: ITPR1 as the Purkinje-cell P400 antigen (Maeda 1990); subtype tissue distribution (Nakagawa 1991; Ross 1992; Taylor 1999); ITPR2 in secretory sweat-gland epithelium (Klar 2014); ITPR3 in pancreas/liver/biliary epithelium (Mangla 2020). No quantitative expression ranking is asserted; GTEx/HPA quantification is deferred to S12.

claim_as_written: Each is a ~58-60 exon gene spanning hundreds of kb
action: STRIKE and replace with measured values
note: FALSE as written. Ensembl 15.12 canonical transcripts: ITPR1 62 exons / 354,174 bp; ITPR2 57 exons / 497,888 bp; ITPR3 58 exons / 76,245 bp. The exon range is 57-62, not 58-60, and ITPR3 spans 76 kb - not "hundreds of kb". The 6.5-fold span range across paralogs is itself a finding for S21.

claim_as_written: ITPR1 carries the alternatively spliced SI, SII and SIII segments that distinguish neuronal from peripheral isoforms
note: Nakagawa 1991 defined SI and SII in mouse; Danoff 1991 showed the SII-containing neuronal versus non-neuronal forms differ in phosphorylation; Nucifora 1995 identified the third (SIII) spliced segment in human ITPR1.

claim_as_written: The IP3R/RyR split predates animals, and both families descend from a single ancestral Ca2+-release channel
note: Mignery 1989 is the original observation that the IP3R sequence resembles the RyR. Cai 2012 places Ca2+-signalling machinery including both channel families before the animal/fungal divergence; Prole 2011 finds IP3R and RyR homologues in parasitic protists; Mackrill 2012 reviews RyR evolution.

claim_as_written: Both families independently expanded to three vertebrate paralogs
note: The three-paralog state of each family is a database fact, but the INDEPENDENCE of the two triplications is exactly open question Q2 and has no verified primary source. It is downgraded to [open] and answered by S7/S13/S16. Asserting it as background would make the project's own conclusion an assumption.

claim_as_written: ITPR1: heterozygous deletions cause SCA15; missense variants cause SCA29
note: van de Leemput 2007 identified the ITPR1 deletion in SCA15 (and the ataxic mouse); Hara 2008 and Marelli 2011 replicated in independent cohorts; Huang 2012 identified missense variants in congenital non-progressive ataxia (SCA29); Zambonin 2017 is the SCA29 case series.

claim_as_written: ITPR1: specific, often C-terminal/pore-proximal variants cause Gillespie syndrome, which behaves as dominant-negative in the tetramer
note: Incomplete as written. Gillespie syndrome is caused by BOTH biallelic (recessive) ITPR1 variants and de novo heterozygous variants (Gerber 2016); only the latter act dominant-negatively via the channel domain (McEntagart 2016). Stating only the dominant-negative mechanism omits half the genetics and would misdirect the S17 constraint analysis.

claim_as_written: ITPR2: homozygous loss of function causes autosomal recessive isolated anhidrosis
note: Klar 2014 is the sole primary source: one consanguineous family, five affected members, a homozygous MISSENSE variant in the pore-forming region that abolishes Ca2+ release - functionally null, not a null allele. Itpr2-/- mice show reduced sweat secretion. The evidence rests on a single family plus the mouse.

claim_as_written: ITPR3: dominant variants are reported in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease / demyelinating neuropathy
note: Ronkko 2020 established the gene-disease relationship (CMT1J); Beijer 2025 found the recurrent p.Thr1424Met in 33 individuals from 9 unrelated families; Cabello-Murgui 2024 [R51] added a further family; Hytonen 2025 is a spontaneous canine null. Molitor 2024 extends the phenotype: p.Arg2524Cys also causes a multisystemic immunodeficiency syndrome, so the ITPR3 phenotype is broader than neuropathy alone.

claim_as_written: Multiple cryo-EM structures of the tetramer exist for rat IP3R1 (apo and ligand-bound) and human IP3R3; RyR1 is one of the best-resolved large channels in the PDB
note: Rat IP3R1: Fan 2015 (apo, 4.7 A), Fan 2018 (ligand-bound states), Baker 2021 (in a lipid bilayer). Human IP3R3: Paknejad 2018 (Ca2+- and IP3-bound states). RyR1: Zalk 2015, Yan 2015, Efremov 2015, all near-atomic in 2015. No PDB IDs are recorded here - S11 discovers the reference panel by RCSB query (background section 6 rule).
